Messages.Author: David Gausebeck
Messages.Body:
If I play Flesh of Marble at superior at the beginning of a round, and during
that round my vampire has 3 normal and two aggravated damage dealt to it (in the
same strike, if it matters), does my vampire take one normal or one aggravated
damage?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:


Officially, he takes only one of the damage - whichever one you want (so, in
the case where you take a mix of normal and agg, you may choose to take
one normal damage *or* one aggravated damage).

Fun, huh?

Messages.Author: Pheersum
Messages.Body:
David Gausebeck wrote:
>
> If I play Flesh of Marble at superior at the beginning of a round, and during
> that round my vampire has 3 normal and two aggravated damage dealt to it (in the
> same strike, if it matters), does my vampire take one normal or one aggravated
> damage?

Under V:TES rules the aggravated damage is applied last in regard to
damage prevention. With 3 points normal and 2 points aggro you would
need 5 points of damage prevention to avoid taking at least 1 point
aggro.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Pheersum <phee...@sb.net> writes:
>David Gausebeck wrote:
>> If I play Flesh of Marble at superior at the beginning of a round, and during
>> that round my vampire has 3 normal and two aggravated damage dealt to it (in the
>> same strike, if it matters), does my vampire take one normal or one aggravated
>> damage?

>Under V:TES rules the aggravated damage is applied last in regard to
>damage prevention. With 3 points normal and 2 points aggro you would
>need 5 points of damage prevention to avoid taking at least 1 point
>aggro.

The normal is applied before the agg if the damage is done at the same time,
correct.

However, *all* of the unprevented damage is applied before you use FoMarble
to shake off all but one. (This is why you can't play prevention cards to
reduce that final 1 to zero - the damage is already applied).

So, when you check FoMarble, you have 3 normal and 2 agg applied to you.
You reduce that to one (whichever one of the five you want - one of the
three normal *or* one of the two agg).

Reference:
From: aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie)
Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Subject: Re: Flesh of Marble
Date: 14 May 1996 20:30:50 GMT
Message-ID: <4naqhq$7...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>

Um, the wording of superior Flesh of Marble is perfectly clear: it lifts
the restriction against preventing aggravated damage. Yes, this means that
if you take a mix of aggravated and non-agg damage, the unprevented point
can come from the non-agg part, but this is really no different from using
Skin of Rock to prevent the agg damage, and taking the rest of it. Aggravated
damage is always applied last, to maximize the chances of burning the vampire;
nothing says it is, or should be, prevented last.

Well, this odd little ruling leads me to think up the following
non-pathological case:

Vamp A and Vamp B are in combat.
B is Quinton who's rushed A with Uncontolled Rage
(Total: 4 agg hand damage).

A plays superior FoMarble.
B plays superior Drawing out the Beast.
No maneuvers.
A strikes: hands for two (using the Beast's +1 hand damage).
B strikes: hands for five agg.
Strikes resolve. (B burns two blood to heal.)
A receives 4 agg and prevents none. 4 agg is applied.
FoMarble can reduce the total damage in a round to one.
This leaves 1 agg. to be paid for (to prevent destruction).
A burns one blood and is about to go to torpor.
Since A is about to go to torpor, the round is ending, so superior Beast
deals one (normal) damage to A.
FoMarble can reduce the total damage in a round to one.
A mix of damage is now taken, and (according to WotC) the vampire can choose
which damage to take.
A chooses to take only the normal damage, naturally, and is no longer going
to torpor.
Since A is still ready, the round isn't over, and superior Beast hasn't
yet dealt any damage, so FoMarble only has 4 agg damage from which to
choose.

-----
Any would-be Net.Rep's out there want to clear this up?

(Without the "ruling" applied to it, the original Jyhad wording reducing
normal and preventing agg wouldn't lead to this catch-22 situation.)

My seat of the pants ruling is that you can't undo an effect already
resolved. Since the damage has already affected the vampire, you can't
undo it. I suppose you could rule that the vamp has already taken 1
damage, he dosen't have to take the additional point, though I'd expect a
"per damage resolution phase" eratta to be added as soon as this little
gem comes up to the Rules Team.

Your opinions, Mawthter? :)

Very good point. However, the damage has been ruled to come at the end
of the round (not after):

From: aa...@hal.COM (Tom Wylie)
Newsgroups: rec.games.deckmaster
Subject: NEW: Rulings summary for Jyhad
Date: 9 Nov 1994 13:11:24 -0800
Message-ID: <39rdts$s...@perv.hal.COM>

Drawing out the Beast:
Does 1 damage at end of round, regardless of how the round ends.

Original card text would mean that the damage from Beast wouldn't be
aggravated in a Dawn Operation if the combat was terminated due to
an Earth Meld. It also leads to a new phase of combat between rounds.
I would actually prefer this ruling - since it allieviates the catch-22,
but...

Currently nothing happens in combat that doesn't happen during a round
of combat (it either happends at the end of a round, at the beginning
of a round, or in the middle - never between rounds).

Beast does its damage during combat, and after the round is after the
combat in this case.
